post.description:
Change the caller's password and sign this session in again.

Requires a valid access token. A wrong current password is a 400 `invalid_current_password`
with a field error on `current_password`; a new password that breaks the registration rules is
a 422 with a field error on `new_password`. Every refresh token of the user is revoked
(other devices sign out when their access token expires), and the response carries new
tokens exactly as `POST /auth/login` does. Attempts share the sign-in throttle (429
`rate_limited` with `Retry-After`).

Client mode: send `X-Client: mobile` without an `Origin` header to get the refresh token in
the response body; every other request is a web client and gets it in the `mtgstats_refresh`
cookie (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/api/v1/auth`) instead.

Exchange a username and password for an access token and a refresh token.

Unknown user, wrong password and inactive account all return the same 401
(``invalid_credentials``). Each sign-in starts a new refresh-token family.

Client mode: send `X-Client: mobile` without an `Origin` header to get the refresh token in
the response body; every other request is a web client and gets it in the `mtgstats_refresh`
cookie (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/api/v1/auth`) instead.

Revoke the current refresh token and clear the cookie.

Needs only the refresh token (cookie for web, body for mobile). Idempotent: a missing,
invalid, unknown or already revoked token still returns 204 and revokes nothing else.

Revoke all of the caller's refresh tokens (every device) and clear the cookie.

Requires a valid access token. Access tokens already issued stay valid until they expire.

get.description:
Return the signed-in user, read from the database on every request.

`is_site_admin` is only for showing or hiding the admin entry in the UI. A deleted or
inactive user gets 401 `invalid_token`.

post.description:
Exchange a refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh token.

The presented token is revoked. Presenting a revoked token (already rotated or signed out)
returns 401 and revokes every token of its family; so does a token of an inactive user. A
missing token is a 401 `unauthenticated`. In web mode a 401 also clears the cookie.

Web clients send the cookie and must use `fetch(..., {credentials: "include"})`; any body token
is ignored. Mobile clients send `{"refresh_token": ...}`.

Client mode: send `X-Client: mobile` without an `Origin` header to get the refresh token in
the response body; every other request is a web client and gets it in the `mtgstats_refresh`
cookie (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/api/v1/auth`) instead.

Create an account from an invite and sign the new user in.

Limited to 30 requests per IP address per 15 minutes by default, shared with the invite
preview (429 `rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`).

The invite is checked first (410 `invite_no_longer_valid`), then the username (409
`username_taken`, and the invite is not used up). Field errors are a 422.

Client mode, as for login: send `X-Client: mobile` without an `Origin` header to get the
refresh token in the response body; every other request is a web client and gets it in the
`mtgstats_refresh` cookie (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/api/v1/auth`).

get.description: Return 200 while the process runs; contacts no dependency.

Return 200 when Postgres and Redis answer, else 503 with the same body shape.

The 503 keeps the ready body (not the error envelope) so monitors see which check failed.
The caller's own invites, newest first, with a derived status. Never the token.

post.description:
Create an invite and return its `https` URL, which is shown only once.

Site admins only (403 otherwise). The body is optional: `expires_in_days` 1-30 (default 7)
and `max_uses` 1-20 (default 1).

Show the inviter's display name and the expiry of an invite. No authentication.

Limited to 30 requests per IP address per 15 minutes by default, shared with registration (429
`rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`). The token is in the body so it never reaches a URL or an
access log. A revoked, expired, used-up or unknown token is a 410 `invite_no_longer_valid`.
Revoke one of the caller's invites. Idempotent. Anyone else's, or unknown, is a 404.
